name: European TTF Natural Gas
summary: European gas (TTF), Day 246. TTF crossed €100/MWh on 28 Oct for the first time since the 2022 crisis and the December contract settled around €103.6 on 30 Oct — up roughly 40% in October and more than three times its pre-war level. Supply is the war's doing: Qatar extended LNG force majeure to the end of December and is shipping perhaps a fifth of pre-war volume, and traders fear Iranian retaliation on Gulf energy if the US strikes after 3 Nov. Demand-side fragility is Europe's own: storage is about 75%, the lowest for the season since records began, with Germany near 62% and some countries already withdrawing. German power is at its highest since mid-2023, and the ECB debated a hike on 29 Oct citing energy. The beneficiaries are US LNG exporters (Cheniere raised guidance) and Qatar's own hedging into US supply. A warm winter or a US–Iran text are the downside paths; a strike on Gulf gas infrastructure the upside.

recent_signals.headline: **TTF CROSSED €100 FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE DECEMBER 2022.** The November contract touched €100–100.9 intraday on 28 Oct (Reuters via RTÉ, Euronews, Il Sole); after the November expiry (~29 Oct) the December contract settled ~€103.6 on 30 Oct (Trading Economics; Investing €103.2–103.9; +5.8% like-for-like). October front-month average ~€86.8; +~36–41% in the month. Drivers (~75% crisis): Qatar force majeure extended to end-December; Ras Laffan ~one-fifth of pre-war; Hormuz LNG risk and post-3-Nov strike fear; plus EU storage ~75% (74.9% on 26 Oct — a crawl, not the 'stall' at 74.6% reported 26 Oct; lowest seasonal since 2011; Germany 61.7%), Asia competition (JKM $30.76 on 22 Oct; ~$34 unverified on 28 Oct), cold-winter risk. German front-year power €159.30 (highest since June 2023). Jørgensen: 'Europe faces another energy crisis.' (CONFIRMED price; intel ISR-A7, MAC-A13; markets C5)

**TTF €97.19 INTRADAY ON 26 OCT — HIGHEST SINCE LATE 2022, ~€3 FROM €100.** ICE close €87.22 (13 Oct; the brief's €86.65 was an indicative tick) → €93.85 (23 Oct) → ~€96 live 26 Oct (+10%). Chain: Qatar LNG still ~0.6 Mt/month (force majeure monthly since March) → JKM $30.76 (22 Oct, highest since Dec 2022) pulls cargoes to Asia → EU storage stalls at 74.6% (lowest for late October since 2009; injections ~+0.09pp/day, some states withdrawing). ~75% crisis / ~25% weather. BofA's Q4 ~€100 tracking; Citi's €56 effectively falsified. (CONFIRMED prices; REPORTED storage; markets C6, intel ISR-A8)

**TTF €73.25 (22 Sep) → €69.81 low (29 Sep) → €84.74 close (12 Oct, +4.05%) → €86.65 (13 Oct) — +18%; highest since late 2022/early 2023.** Drivers: Hormuz attacks on LNG carriers (Maran Gas Mystras hit 4–5 Oct) and rerouting; **Qatar October LNG tracking 0.6 Mt vs 1.6 Mt in September** (Kpler); QatarEnergy force majeure extended; North-Asian LNG ~3× pre-war bidding cargoes away; cold second-half-October forecast. EU storage (AGSI+ trackers) 70.87% (26 Sep) → 73.61% (10 Oct) vs ~83% a year ago; Germany ~60%; ~+0.20pp/day → ~78% by 1 Nov, short of the relaxed 80% target. Commission (8 Oct): system 'sufficiently flexible', no emergency measures; energy ministers 29 Oct. **The Saudi crude cut reversed for November while TTF rose — the gas cascade runs on Qatar LNG, not Saudi crude.** Baseline correction: 22-Sep storage was ~69.5–70%, not 68%. Citi Q4 €56 (relayed, low confidence). — CONFIRMED (prices, storage).

Path: €59 (31 Jul) → €82 (10 Sep) → €73.25. The €70 cascade-intensity trigger (sustained 5 sessions) has been met since early Sep; a close <€70 would de-activate it. (yfinance TTF=F; Bloomberg; TE; OilPrice) — CONFIRMED.

(2) **But the structural floor holds**: +4.4% MoM, +25% YoY vs the ~€31.20 pre-crisis baseline. Qatar Ras Laffan Trains 4/6 (12.8 mtpa, ~17% Qatar LNG) force majeure is a 3-5yr recovery — NOT contingent on Iran deal architecture — so the YoY premium is durable. C4 paper-physical non-confirmation: even on a clean signed deal, the physical gas/LNG cost stack bleeds out over 6-12 weeks, not in a session; 3 LNG vessels is not a reopening. (3) **Trigger**: 'TTF crosses €70/MWh sustained 5 sessions' remains NOT ACTIVATED — €46.63 vs €70 = €23 gap, FURTHER from threshold than May 22's €48.69. (4) **B1 context**: the EU formally ADOPTED a Hormuz-disruption sanctions framework May 22 (CONFIRMED across multiple European outlets — upgrades the prior single-source Al Jazeera flag), enabling travel bans / asset freezes but with NO designations yet. A Hormuz-sanctions architecture being erected at the moment a US-Iran deal would reopen the strait and waive US oil sanctions is a transatlantic-divergence cross-current. (5) **Henry Hub $3.02 FROZEN** (US Memorial Day — NYMEX did not settle; do NOT read as a live Monday move). **Reversibility**: shallow on deal-anticipation (-€2 to -€5/MWh, realised today); structural floor ~€40-42 absent durable Qatar capacity return.

**GAS IS WHERE THE WAR IS ACTUALLY WINNING — oil has buffers, gas has none.** TTF **EUR57.49-58.91/MWh (17 Jul, two feeds disagree on the print), +29% to +42% in three weeks** and a four-month high; **JKM Asian spot jumped 18.5% IN A SINGLE DAY on 16 Jul to $19.93/MMBtu.** The physical picture is worse than the price: **EU storage 53% full vs a 75% five-year norm — the lowest in FIFTEEN YEARS** — with July injections at a six-year low and net injections since April covering only **40% of winter need**; the mandatory target has been relaxed 90%->80% plus 4% deviation. Two self-reinforcing mechanisms. (1) The Qatari loss is NOT a spike: **12.8 mtpa (17% of the 77 mtpa system) offline for 3-5 YEARS**, force majeure in its FOURTH consecutive month and extended to Italy's Edison through early September (21 cargoes lost Apr-Sep), and QatarEnergy has **PAUSED its restart ramp** after one of its own tankers was hit — the constraint is Hormuz safety, not repairs. Its guidance of 50% of capacity within a month of safe passage / ~80% within two months is entirely gated on that. (2) **US LNG is being pulled AWAY from Europe by Asia: 41.9% of US exports went to Europe in June, the first time below 50% in ~2 years, down from 50.2% in May.** JKM's one-day 18.5% jump is Asian buyers outbidding Europe for the marginal cargo — **Europe's shortfall and Asia's bid are the same trade.** CONFIRMED.

**TTF broke to a new cycle high — EUR58.74/MWh on Monday 20 July, +2.3% on the day and +19.8% since 8 July**, with the UK equivalent +3.52%, both the highest since 23 March. **The proximate trigger was the Hormuz tanker fire**, and the physical driver is precise: **no laden Qatari LNG carrier appears to have transited Hormuz in nearly two weeks.** EU gas storage is **~51.8% (12 July)** against ~54% a year ago and roughly **14 points below the five-year average — the lowest in 15 years**, with the mandatory target already relaxed from 90% to 80% plus a 4% deviation allowance. Qatar's 12.8 mtpa (17% of its system) remains offline with force majeure live; Asian buyers had *expected* a July lapse in the force majeure — that expectation is **not** a confirmed lapse and should not be reported as one. **Gas remains the channel with no buffer: no SPR equivalent, no OPEC spare capacity, no pipeline bypass.** ⚠️ JKM could not be refreshed — the 16 July print of $19.93/MMBtu is **STALE**. CONFIRMED (TTF) / REPORTED (storage, secondary).

**New cycle high — EUR61.37/MWh (22 Jul), +2.8% d/d and +44.8% over 30 days**, above the EUR58.74 of 20 July. The driver is unchanged and physical: no laden Qatari LNG carrier has transited Hormuz in ~2 weeks. EU storage ~51.8% (STALE — could not refresh; 15-year low stands), mandatory target already relaxed 90%->80%. Pakistan paid its highest LNG spot since 2022 (17 Jul), evidence of Asian scramble for non-Qatari cargo. Gas remains the channel with no buffer, and it is now the clearest single price expression of the Qatari outage. CONFIRMED.

New cycle high — EUR63.75/MWh (23 Jul), +EUR2.38 over EUR61.37, still driven by the absence of any laden Qatari LNG through Hormuz. EU storage ~53% (vs ~64% a year ago; refill lagging into a 15-year-low base). The ECB explicitly cited energy risk in pausing today. Gas remains the channel with no buffer and the clearest single price expression of the Qatari outage. JKM stale at $19.93 (16 Jul). CONFIRMED (TTF) / STALE (storage/JKM).
